thesis: BHP's FY2026 result was solid - dividend up to US$1.72, net debt down to US$8.69B - but the commodity mix is turning: iron ore is approaching the US$90/t level that has historically triggered earnings downgrades, and copper strength is what has been carrying the stock. Add a price feed I could not verify and a live RBA hike on 29 Sep, and there is no edge in adding here.
bull_case: FY2026 results (18 Aug 2026): annual dividend raised to US$1.72 per share, the highest in four years, with net debt down to US$8.69B, near the bottom of the target range - a balance sheet with room. Copper has been the driver, with the stock reported at a record in mid-June 2026 on the copper rally and up strongly over 12 months; JPMorgan carries a Buy with a A$67 target. The packet trend agrees: close above SMA50 above SMA200, score +0.41, RSI 55, ATR 2.5%. Copper is the one commodity with a genuine multi-year supply deficit story attached to electrification.
bear_case: Iron ore is still the profit engine and it is approaching the US$90/t psychological floor, a level that historically triggers significant downward earnings revisions; sell-side work published this cycle argues neither the copper nor the iron ore outlook is supportive. Momentum is already fading - 3m momentum of just +5.9% is the weakest of our holdings bar SPY - and BHP opened flat then fell ~2% on Fri 4 Sep as miners dragged the ASX 200 down to 9,006. China demand is the whole thesis and the trade backdrop is deteriorating: China publicly hit back at the G20 over export reliance on 3 Sep. Broker targets straddle the price (RBC Hold A$60, Macquarie Hold A$55), which is the definition of no edge. Data-integrity flag: the packet prices this at 44.8519, but dated reports through Aug-Sep 2026 put it materially higher (around A$63.5 in mid-Aug 2026, with broker targets between A$55 and A$67). I could not reconcile this from the session - Yahoo Finance egress is blocked here, so the desk's own price source cannot be re-queried independently. Until the ASX feed is reconciled, any level-based call on this symbol (entries, stops, invalidation) is built on a number I could not verify.
catalysts: Iron ore holding or losing the US$90/t level
China stimulus or further trade escalation after the 3 Sep G20 exchange
29 Sep 2026 RBA decision and the AUD
risks: Unverified price feed: the packet level conflicts with dated market reports
Iron ore below US$90/t triggering consensus earnings downgrades
Single-commodity concentration despite the copper story
AUD strength on an RBA hike reducing AUD-translated earnings
invalidation: Reconcile the ASX price feed first. Thereafter: the bear case confirms on iron ore closing below US$90/t for a week, or a break of the packet's SMA50; constructive again only if copper makes new highs while iron ore holds above US$95/t.
